# Independent Verification and Execution Gate

This page covers what happens between "here is a script" and "here are results". When the AI agent finishes writing a script (see [Code Generation and Agent Repair Loop](code-generation-repair.md)), it says its tests passed. Auto-Mate does not take its word for that. It checks the code itself, records exactly what it checked and on which Python setup, and shows you a report. It then asks you before the script touches your real file. After the script runs, it asks you whether the result is actually what you wanted.

No AI is contacted at any point in this feature. Checking, approving, running, and reviewing all happen on your computer with fixed, repeatable tools. Your file is sent to no one.

Three things to know before you rely on any of this:

- **The script is given a copy of your file, and nothing in this preview prevents generated code from reaching other files on this computer.** The copy protects your original from a script with a bug. It does not protect anything from a script that means harm. When the script runs, it has the same access to your computer as Auto-Mate itself.
- **Passing checks and tests on made-up data is evidence about the code's shape, not proof it will work on your file.** The checks read the code and the tests run on synthetic rows built from your file's description. A script that passes all of them can still fail on your real data or produce wrong numbers.
- **The separate checker environment (`verify-env/`), `ruff --isolated`, the explicit bandit config and ini files, and the copied input are hygiene, not a security boundary.** They keep the checks honest and protect the original file from accidents. They do not limit what the script can reach. Restricted execution is still required before any pilot with target users, and the technology for it has not been chosen.

## What It Does

### From a finished script to a result

1. **Checking.** When code generation ends with a final version, the run moves to checking. The conversation shows **Checking the code…**.
2. **The report.** Auto-Mate runs seven checks in a fixed order and shows a one-line verdict. For example: **All checks passed.**, **No blocking problems found; 2 advisory findings to review.**, or **This code can't run yet: 1 high-severity security finding and 1 failing test.**
3. **A blocked run stops here.** If anything blocks, the run ends as failed with code `VERIFICATION_BLOCKED` and the verdict as its message. There is no button that runs it anyway.
4. **The approval gate.** If nothing blocks, the run waits for you, with no time limit. A panel headed **Before you run** shows what will happen. Nothing runs until you select **Run it**.
5. **The run.** The script runs once, against a verified copy of your file.
6. **The review.** If the script finished and wrote everything it said it would, the run waits again. The panel asks **Did this do what you wanted?** The run counts as completed only when you say yes.

### The seven checks

The checks always run in this order, and every check appears in the report every time. A check that did not run is shown as skipped, never left out, so a missing check can never look like a passed one.

| # | Check | What it looks for | What it protects against |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `integrity` | Recomputes each stored file's SHA-256 fingerprint and the version's overall fingerprint, and compares them with the ones recorded when the version was sealed. Rebuilds the made-up test data from its recorded seed and checks that it comes out byte-for-byte the same. Then rewrites the files to disk from the database. | Checking or running code that is not the code that was sealed, and relying on a test result nobody can repeat. If this check fails, the other checks do not run and are shown as skipped. |
| 2 | `contract_entrypoint` | The file the script says it starts from exists and is a script file, not a test file. | A run that cannot start. |
| 3 | `contract_inputs` | Every column the script says it needs exists in your file, according to the stored profile of your file. It compares names and types only and never reads a cell value. It also checks that each file and sheet the script names is attached. Skipped when the task has no attached files. | A script that will certainly fail because a column or file it needs is not there. |
| 4 | `contract_outputs` | The script's list of outputs can be read and is not empty. Every output is a plain file name (no folders, no `..`, no absolute path), has a type Auto-Mate knows, and appears only once. | Outputs written outside the output folder, outputs that can never be shown, and ambiguous results. |
| 5 | `lint` | `ruff` looks for syntax errors, undefined names, likely bugs, and risky patterns (rule families `E9`, `F`, `B`, and `S`). | Code that is broken before it even starts. |
| 6 | `security` | `bandit` scans for known dangerous patterns, such as running shell commands built from text. A file bandit cannot read counts as a blocking finding, because an unchecked file is not a clean one. | Code with high-confidence, high-severity security problems. |
| 7 | `tests` | Auto-Mate runs the agent's pytest tests **itself**, against the rebuilt test data, rather than trusting the result the agent reported. A pass needs a zero exit code **and** a pytest summary Auto-Mate recognizes with no failures. A zero exit with no readable summary does not count as a pass. | Trusting the model's report on the model's own work. |

The checks read and run only the code and the made-up test data. Your real file is not opened while checking. Each check stores up to 200 findings; any more are counted and the summary says so.

### What blocks and what is only shown

A finding either **blocks** the run or is **advisory**. The rules below are provisional against open decision D14.

These block the run:

- The app-driven test re-run did not pass: a test failed, or the result could not be trusted.
- A `bandit` finding at HIGH severity and HIGH confidence.
- A `ruff` finding whose rule starts with `E9`, `F6`, `F7`, or `F82`, or whose code is exactly `invalid-syntax`. These mean syntax errors, statement errors, and undefined names. Current ruff reports a syntax error as `invalid-syntax` rather than an `E9` rule, so that code is listed on its own.
- Any failed `integrity`, `contract_entrypoint`, or `contract_outputs` check.
- A missing required column or a missing input file in `contract_inputs`.
- Any check that could not run (`errored`). "We could not check this" never counts as "this passed". Examples: ruff or bandit could not be prepared or their report could not be read, a check ran past its time limit, or pytest could not run.

These are advisory:

- Every other `ruff` finding, such as an unused import (`F401`).
- Every other `bandit` finding, such as MEDIUM severity or MEDIUM confidence.
- A column type difference in `contract_inputs`. For example, the script treats a column as `integer` but your file looks like `decimal`. Scripts usually still work in that case, so it is shown but does not block.
- A check shown as skipped, such as `contract_inputs` when no file is attached.

Advisory findings appear in the report and in the approval panel. You must confirm you have read them before **Run it** becomes available.

Whether each check and finding blocked is stored with it when it is recorded. A later change to these rules does not rewrite why an earlier run was allowed.

### Results are tied to the exact code and the exact Python setup

A check result applies to two things:

- **The code**, by the fingerprint (SHA-256 digest) of the files that were checked.
- **The runtime**, by a fingerprint covering the Python version, the `uv` version, the operating system and processor type, and the version of every installed package.

If both are unchanged, Auto-Mate reuses the earlier result instead of checking again. If Python, `uv`, or any package changes, the old result no longer covers the run and the code is checked again. The gate names the concrete change rather than showing a hash. For example: **Python changed from 3.12.4 to 3.13.1**, **pandas changed from 2.3.1 to 2.4.0**, or **openpyxl 3.1.5 was added**. The earlier result stays stored, because it is still true about the earlier setup.

The report and the approval panel include a runtime line such as **Checked against Python 3.12.4 on Windows (x64). If Python or an installed package changes, the code is checked again before it can run.**

### The approval gate

Every run that passes its checks stops at this gate. There is no setting to skip it.

The **Before you run** panel shows:

- **It will read:** each attached file by its original name and size.
- **It says it will write:** each declared output by file name, type, and title.
- **What was checked:** the check summary and the verdict.
- **The runtime line:** what the code was checked against.
- **The caveats.** These three sentences are shown word for word:
  > The checks and tests ran on synthetic rows shaped like your file, not on your file itself. Passing them is evidence about the code's shape, not proof it will work on your data.
  >
  > The script is handed a copy of your file, so the original is not the file it opens. The copy guards against a buggy script; it is not a security boundary.
  >
  > This preview runs generated code without an isolation boundary, with the same access this application has. Nothing here prevents it from reaching other files on this computer.
- **A confirmation box**, only when there are advisory findings: **I have read the 2 advisory findings in the report above.**
- **Run it** and **Cancel**. **Cancel** ends the run as cancelled (`aborted`).

Your approval covers exactly three things: the code's fingerprint, the runtime fingerprint, and a fingerprint of exactly what the panel showed you. If any of them changes, the approval no longer applies. That can happen in three ways:

| What changed | What you see | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The page is out of date | `APPROVAL_INTENT_MISMATCH`: "This page is out of date: what the run will do has changed since it was shown. Reload it and review again before running." | What the server would run now differs from what your page shows. Nothing is recorded, and the panel reloads itself. Review it again. |
| The Python setup changed | The approval is not recorded. The panel says **The environment changed since the check, so it is being checked again:** and lists each change. | Auto-Mate probes the runtime again when you select **Run it**. If it moved since the check, the code goes back to checking. You are asked again only if the new check passes. |
| The code or runtime changed after you approved | `APPROVAL_STALE`: "The approval no longer applies because the code changed after you approved it" (or "the Python environment changed after you approved it"). The run ends as failed. | Just before the script starts, Auto-Mate recomputes the code fingerprint from the stored files and probes the runtime again. Both are compared with your stored approval. If either differs, no process is started. |

### The run

After **Run it**:

1. Auto-Mate copies each attached file into `runs/<run id>/input/` under its stored name. It then recomputes the copy's SHA-256 and compares it with the fingerprint recorded at upload. If they differ, the run stops before the script starts, with `INPUT_COPY_MISMATCH`. The message names the file by position ("file 1"), not by name.
2. It empties `runs/<run id>/output/`, rewrites the code from the database, and makes the gate comparison described above.
3. It starts the script's entry point with `AUTOMATE_INPUT_DIR` pointing at the copies and `AUTOMATE_OUTPUT_DIR` pointing at the output folder. The script runs with the same Python runner and environment as the test runs. The page shows **This is running on your computer with the same access this application has.**
4. The script must write its outputs into the output folder and list them in `manifest.json` there.

**A zero exit code is not acceptance.** A run is treated as finished only when all three of these are true: the script exited with code 0, it wrote a valid `manifest.json`, and every file listed there exists. The run then waits for your review. Otherwise it ends as failed with one of these messages (code `RUN_OUTPUT_MISSING`):

- "The script stopped with an error (exit code 1) before it finished. Its output is shown below."
- "The script finished but did not say what it produced."
- "The script said it would produce 2 files, but 1 of them was not written."
- "The script ran longer than 15 min and was stopped. Nothing it produced has been kept as a result."
- "The script could not be started: uv or Python is not available, or the Python environment is not prepared."

A result panel shows the outcome in words, the declared outputs with type and size, and the script's output under **Show the script's output**. Output on each of the two streams (normal output and error output) is capped at 1 MiB. When the cap is hit, the first half and the last half are kept, a marker shows where the middle was removed, and the panel says **The output was long, so only its beginning and end were kept.** The script's output can contain values from your file. It is stored in the local database, never written to the application log, and never sent to an AI.

Opening, viewing, and downloading the output files arrive with the next feature (FEAT-109). For now the panel says **Viewing and downloading these files arrives with the next feature; for now they are listed here by name.**

### The review

A successful run shows **Did this do what you wanted?** with two answers:

- **Yes, this is what I wanted** The run becomes completed. On this path, completed means a person said so.
- **No — here's what's wrong.** A box opens: **What is wrong? The next attempt will be told exactly this.** Feedback is required, cannot be blank, and can be up to 2,000 characters. **Try again with this** does the following:
  - The run is marked rejected and your feedback is stored with it.
  - A **new run** of the same task is created, linked to the rejected one, with trigger `feedback`. Your feedback becomes its guidance and is sent to the AI provider as your own words. Your file-description approval and pre-flight answers are reused, as with a guidance retry.
  - The rejected run is not changed. Its checks, approval, run record, and conversation stay readable.

If the new run cannot start because the only active slot is in use (`EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED`), your rejection still stands and is not undone.

**How to write feedback that gets a better retry.** The agent has never seen your real file or the output files. It only knows what you tell it. Say concretely what was wrong:

- Which rows: "rows where Region is blank were dropped; keep them as 'Unknown'."
- Which columns: "the Total column should be summed, not averaged."
- Which values: "March shows 0 but should be about 41,000."
- Which rule: "a week starts on Monday", "amounts are in euros with a comma as the decimal mark".
- What the output should look like: file type, columns, grouping, sort order.

One or two concrete corrections work better than restating the whole request. Do not paste rows of your real data: everything you type is sent to the AI provider as written.

### Cancelling

One control and one route cancel every stage: **Cancel run**, or `POST /api/executions/:id/abort`.

- **While checking:** any running `ruff`, `bandit`, or pytest process is stopped. The check pass is recorded as stopped, and the run ends as cancelled.
- **At the approval gate or the review:** the run ends as cancelled immediately. No approval is recorded and no retry is created.
- **While the script runs:** the script and every process it started are stopped, and the run ends as cancelled.

Shutting the server down cancels checking and running the same way.

### After a server restart

- A run **waiting for your approval** or **waiting for your review** survives a restart unchanged. These waits have nothing in memory, and your pending decision is not the server's to discard. After the restart you can still approve, and the script runs normally.
- A run interrupted **while checking** ends as failed with `EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED`: "This run was interrupted while its code was being checked. Start it again to retry."
- A run interrupted **while the script was running** ends as failed with `EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED`: "This run was interrupted while the script was running on your file. Start it again to retry."

A run waiting at either gate does not hold the single active slot, so other tasks can run meanwhile.

## How to Use It

### In the browser

1. Describe the task, attach a file, and approve the review as usual. Code generation runs and chooses a final version.
2. Wait for **Checking the code…** to change into the report under **Code check results**. Open a check to see its findings, grouped by file.
3. If the run is blocked, read the verdict. Start again with guidance, or start a new task.
4. At **Before you run**, read what it will read and write, the checks, the runtime line, and the three caveats. If there are advisory findings, tick the confirmation box. Select **Run it**, or **Cancel**.
5. When the run finishes, read **What it produced** and the script's output.
6. Answer **Did this do what you wanted?**

### Use the local API

```sh
# The latest check pass for run 9, with every check and finding.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/verification

# Check again (for example after the Python setup changed). Allowed while checking or waiting for approval.
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/verify

# What the approval panel shows, and the digest an approval must carry.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/intent

# Approve exactly that intent.
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/approval \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"intentDigest":"<64 hex characters from /intent>","decision":"approved","acknowledgedWarnings":true}'

# The run record: status, exit code, captured output, declared outputs.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/run

# Reject the result with feedback; a new linked run starts.
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/review \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"verdict":"rejected","feedback":"The Total column should be summed per month, not averaged."}'
```

## Inputs and Outputs

### REST routes

| Method and path | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/verification` | A positive run id | The latest check pass: its id, run and version ids, `contentDigest`, `runtimeFingerprint`, `runtime` (Python, uv, platform, arch, packages) and `runtimeDescription`, `status`, `blockingCount`, `advisoryCount`, `summary`, timings, `checks` in the fixed check order (key, status, whether it blocked, summary, detail, duration), and `findings` (check, rule code, severity, confidence, relative file path, line, column, message, whether it blocks). `VERIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` before any pass. |
| `POST /api/executions/:id/verify` | None | `202 { "status": "verifying" }`. Checks again with a fresh runtime probe; an unchanged code-and-runtime pair reuses its result. Allowed only while checking or waiting for approval. |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/intent` | A positive run id | `{ intent, intentDigest }`. `intent` is everything the approval panel shows: code version (short digest, file count, line count, entry point), the agent's summary, inputs (original name, size, short SHA-256, sheets), declared outputs, checks, verdict, counts, test totals and synthetic row count, runtime, and `caveats`. `VERIFICATION_BLOCKED` when the latest pass did not allow the run. |
| `POST /api/executions/:id/approval` | `{ intentDigest, decision: "approved" \| "cancelled", acknowledgedWarnings }`; no other fields | `{ outcome, approvalId, runtimeChanges, status }`. `outcome` is `approved` (the run starts; `status` is `executing`), `cancelled` (`aborted`), or `reverify` (the runtime changed; `approvalId` is `null`, `runtimeChanges` lists the changes, and `status` is `verifying`). |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/run` | A positive run id | The run record: status (`running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `errored`, `timed_out`, `aborted`), `exitCode`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `outputTruncated`, `manifestPresent`, `declaredOutputs` (file name, type, title, description, byte size, whether present), declared and produced counts, inputs (upload id, size, short SHA-256), the code and runtime fingerprints it ran with, and timings. `RUN_NOT_FOUND` before the run starts. |
| `POST /api/executions/:id/review` | `{ verdict: "accepted" \| "rejected", feedback? }`; feedback is required and non-blank for a rejection, at most 2,000 characters | `{ status, retryExecutionId }`: `completed` and `null`, or `rejected` and the new run's id. |

No response contains a full path on your computer. Findings use paths relative to the code folder, and runs name outputs by file name only. The four `POST` routes apply the same browser-origin check as other state-changing routes, so a web page in your own browser cannot approve a run for you. A `curl` request without an `Origin` header is accepted.

### Conversation events

Four new entries appear in the conversation. None of them carries finding text, file contents, or script output.

| Event | Carries |
| --- | --- |
| `verification_finished` | The pass id, version id, status, blocking and advisory counts, the one-line verdict, and the runtime description. |
| `approval_decided` | The approval id, `approved` or `cancelled`, and whether advisory findings were acknowledged. |
| `run_finished` | The run id, status, exit code, duration, declared and produced output counts, and whether output was cut. |
| `review_decided` | `accepted` or `rejected`, and for a rejection the new run's id. |

### Error codes

Errors use the standard envelope `{ error: { code, message, correlationId } }`.

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VERIFICATION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The run has not been checked yet. |
| `VERIFICATION_STALE` | 409 | The earlier check no longer applies to this code and runtime, and the code is being checked again. The message names the concrete changes when known. |
| `VERIFICATION_BLOCKED` | 409, or a run result | The latest check pass did not allow the run. As a run result, the message is the verdict, for example "This code can't run yet: 1 failing test." |
| `EXECUTION_NOT_APPROVED` | 409 | The run is not waiting for approval (the message names its actual state), or it has not been approved. |
| `APPROVAL_INTENT_MISMATCH` | 409 | Your page is out of date. Reload and review again. |
| `APPROVAL_STALE` | 409, or a run result | The approval no longer applies because the code, the Python environment, or what the run will do changed after you approved. No script was started. |
| `RUN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The script has not been started on your file for this run. |
| `RUN_OUTPUT_MISSING` | 422, or a run result | The script failed, timed out, could not start, did not write `manifest.json`, or did not write every file it declared. The message says which. |
| `CHECKER_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | `uv` is missing or the `ruff`/`bandit` environment could not be prepared. The message gives the install command or the reason. During a check pass, this makes `lint` and `security` show as not run, which blocks. |
| `REVIEW_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | There is no result waiting for your review. The message names the run's actual state. |
| `INPUT_COPY_MISMATCH` | 409, or a run result | The copy of your file made for this run did not match the upload, so the script was not started. Upload the file again and start a new run. |

Related codes from earlier features also appear: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400) for a malformed id or body, blank rejection feedback, feedback over 2,000 characters, or advisory findings that were not acknowledged. `ORIGIN_REJECTED` (403) is returned for a foreign browser origin. `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` (404) and `EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED` (409) also appear. `EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED` is used after a restart.

### Where files are stored

Auto-Mate adds two entries under its data folder:

```text
~/.automate/                        (or the folder in AUTOMATE_HOME)
├── verify-env/                     the code checkers, kept apart from the code they check
│   ├── pyproject.toml              ruff and bandit, exact versions; written by Auto-Mate, do not edit
│   ├── bandit.yaml, bandit.ini     Auto-Mate's own bandit settings; nothing is skipped
│   ├── uv.lock
│   └── .venv/
└── runs/<run id>/
    ├── input/<stored file name>    a verified copy of your file; AUTOMATE_INPUT_DIR
    ├── output/                     what the script wrote, plus manifest.json; AUTOMATE_OUTPUT_DIR
    └── verify/                     rebuilt test data and scratch space for the test re-run
```

The checkers run from inside `verify-env/`, never from the folder being checked. `ruff` runs with `--isolated`, and `bandit` gets explicit `-c` and `--ini` files. Settings files placed beside the generated code therefore cannot switch checks off. The first check pass installs `ruff` and `bandit` into `verify-env/` with `uv`, which needs network access once. The versions are pinned (ruff 0.16.8, bandit 1.9.4) and are provisional against open decision D05.

## Configuration and Permissions

Set these environment variables before starting the server. All six are **provisional against open decision D14**; the defaults may change when D14 is decided. A value that is not a whole number within the allowed range stops the server at startup with `CONFIGURATION_ERROR`, and the message names the variable.

| Variable | Default | Allowed values | What it limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTOMATE_VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` (5 minutes) | 1 or more | One whole check pass. When it runs out, the running check is stopped and the pass ends as timed out, which blocks. |
| `AUTOMATE_LINT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` (1 minute) | 1 or more | One `ruff` run. |
| `AUTOMATE_SECURITY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `120000` (2 minutes) | 1 or more | One `bandit` run. |
| `AUTOMATE_SCRIPT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `900000` (15 minutes) | 1 or more | The script's run on your file. When it runs out, the script and everything it started are stopped. |
| `AUTOMATE_MAX_RUN_OUTPUT_BYTES` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | 1 to 67,108,864 | Bytes of normal output and of error output kept from one run, first half and last half. |
| `AUTOMATE_MAX_REVIEW_FEEDBACK_CHARS` | `2000` | 1 to 2,000 | Characters in rejection feedback. It can be lowered but not raised, because the request itself rejects anything longer than 2,000. |

The test re-run in the `tests` check uses the existing `AUTOMATE_TEST_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`. Preparing `verify-env/` uses the existing `AUTOMATE_UV_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS`.

**Prerequisites.** The same `uv` and Python 3.11 or newer that code generation needs. `ruff` and `bandit` are not host prerequisites, because Auto-Mate installs them itself.

**Permissions.** This is a single-user local application with no accounts or roles. Anyone who can use it locally can read check reports, approve a run, and review results. Rejecting a result starts a new run, which uses provider credit.

## Limitations

- **No isolation.** The script runs with Auto-Mate's own access to your computer and can reach files other than its input copy, including your original upload. `verify-env/`, `--isolated`, the explicit bandit config and ini, and the copied input are hygiene, not a security boundary. Restricted execution is required before any target-user pilot.
- **Checks are evidence, not proof.** The static checks read the code, and the tests run on synthetic rows. None of them shows that the script is correct for your real file. That is why the review step exists.
- **No AI code review.** Only the deterministic checks described here run. A second model reviewing the code was deliberately not adopted, because its answers cannot be repeated. It is tracked for reconsideration in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.
- **The run step is minimal.** It has a time limit and an output cap, but no memory or resource limits, no locked dependency policy, and no concurrency of its own. FEAT-108 replaces it.
- **Outputs cannot be opened yet.** Output files are listed by name, type, and size only. Viewing and downloading arrive with FEAT-109.
- **No automatic repair after a failed run.** A failed real run stops and tells you why. The script's output is never sent back to the agent.
- **Nothing expires.** `runs/` folders hold a full copy of every input file plus the outputs, and nothing cleans them up in this build.
